issues.failure_explanation: The assumption y0≠0 does not ensure that its coordinates, or later solution coordinates, are nonzero. For A=0 and y0=tilde y0=(1,0), the second componentwise errors are 0/0. Nonzero initial coordinates can also cross zero during evolution. Consequently, the componentwise definitions and the unconditional comparisons involving their maxima are not defined on all admitted inputs.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify an extended-error convention at zero denominators, handling 0/0 separately, and restrict comparison 3) to nonzero solution coordinates. Alternatively, explicitly state the nonvanishing-coordinate hypotheses for these comparisons.
issues.overall_effect: The normwise-to-componentwise comparisons in Section 2.1 require an additional domain convention; the normwise conditioning results are unaffected.
issues.title: Componentwise relative errors are undefined at admitted zero components
issues.why_classification: A routine local domain convention or zero-coordinate case split preserves the normwise theory and all substantive comparisons where finite componentwise relative errors exist.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: let $w^{(1)}$  (a complex row vector)  and $v^{(1)}$ (a complex column vector)  be left and right, respectively, eigenvectors corresponding to $\lambda_1$

issues.failure_explanation: The new eigenvector definitions do not require wv=1. The actual spectral term uses vw/(wv), whereas the defined oscillating terms use vw and therefore retain an arbitrary phase. In the Euclidean norm, take A=[[0,-2],[1/2,0]], eigenvalue i, v=(2i,1)^T, w=(1/4,i/2), y0=e1 and z0=e2. These satisfy the stated requirements and wv=i. At every t=2πk, the actual directional condition number is 1, but the theorem's product is 4. Independent rescaling also changes f_j/f_1 arbitrarily in the onset theorem, although the underlying condition numbers do not change.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Explicitly retain the dual Jordan/eigenvector construction from Section 3: choose the left vectors from the inverse right-vector basis, so w^(j)v^(j)=1, and use these consistently in Sections 4–5.
issues.overall_effect: The complex time-dependent asymptotic formulas and the subsequent onset error bounds are not valid for the eigenvectors permitted by the stated definitions.
issues.title: The complex asymptotic formula requires an unstated dual eigenvector normalization
issues.why_classification: This standard, always-available normalization is a local repair that preserves every matrix regime, asymptotic formula, and onset guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $r_1,\ldots,r_q$ be the distinct decreasing real parts of the eigenvalues of $A$.

Both onset criteria then contain log(0) and a maximum over an empty index set. No real-valued bound is defined, although the onset theorem itself has empty remainder sums in this case.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State separately that q=1 gives zero remainder and exact agreement with the asymptotic condition numbers for all times; impose q≥2 only on the logarithmic criteria.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised explicit onset tests cannot be used in the permitted one-band cases.
issues.title: The logarithmic onset criteria omit the single-spectral-band case

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Using the Euclidean norm as vector norm, we have $V_1=0.9988$ and $W_1=0.9986$.

issues.failure_explanation: The example evaluates a different expression from the term in the cited onset bound. That bound contains (1/2)log(1/(1−V1)), not (1/2)log(1/sqrt(1−V1)). The correct contribution is approximately 3.37, twice the reported 1.6844. Its combination with −2.8115 is therefore positive, about 0.56, rather than negative.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the actual term from epsilonc<, recompute its numerical value, and update the comparison with the negative log(f2/f1) contribution.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: As in Section \ref{NAsy} (see the ratio (\ref{ratioR})), we set $T$ to fifty times the characteristic time, i.e. $T=50$, and the maximum is determined using $1000$ equally spaced sampling points.

issues.failure_explanation: The grid maxima need not approximate the defined continuous maxima. For Annormal with a=5000 and y0=(-1,0.1), in the infinity norm put u=5000(1−exp(−t)). Then K/K∞=(4990/5001)(1+u)/max(|u−10|,exp(−t)). Its maximum is 1+55000/5001≈11.998 at t=log(5001/4990)≈0.002202. The approximately 0.05-spaced grid instead sees a maximum of only about 1.045. Thus the stated procedure can miss an order-of-magnitude peak inside its own observation interval.

failure_location.quote: The maxima are determined using $1000$ equally spaced sampling points over the interval $[0,T]$, i.e. with a stepsize $\frac{1}{20}$ of the characteristic time.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use error-controlled continuous maximization and recompute the tables. For example, the defining formula gives |log K(t)−log K(s)|≤2||A||||t−s|, which can certify inter-sample errors; the periodic asymptotic denominator must likewise be maximized with error control.
issues.overall_effect: The continuous-maximum statistics in Sections 8–9 and their use as evidence for small transient overshoots are unreliable. The analytical condition-number formulas are unaffected.
issues.title: The fixed-grid maximum estimator misses substantial transient peaks
issues.why_classification: Repair requires a certified maximization procedure and reoptimization of the numerical experiments, but not a new asymptotic theory.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $T$ is fifty times the characteristic time $\widehat{t}=\frac{1}{\vert r_1\vert}$.

issues.failure_explanation: Even if the maxima on [0,T] were computed exactly, the experiments provide no control of the remaining time interval. Replacing A by A−cI leaves K(t,y0) and its asymptotic version unchanged, but changes the chosen terminal time to 50/|r1−c|, which tends to zero as c grows. Thus an unchanged transient peak can lie outside the tested window. The paper's own onset criteria depend on spectral gaps and coefficient ratios, not merely on |r1|, and are not applied to certify these experimental horizons.
